title: FOLLOW THE ARK, KEEP YOUR DISTANCE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: After three days the officers went throughout the camp, giving orders to the people: "When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, and the Levitical priests carrying it, you are to move out from your positions and follow it. Then you will know which way to go, since you have never been this way before. But keep a distance of about two thousand cubits between you and the ark; do not go near it." — Josh 3:2-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The instructions are simple but profound. The people were to follow the ark of the covenant — the symbol of God's presence among them — because, as God tenderly reminds them, "you have never been this way before." What a comfort that must have been. They were heading into unknown territory, and God essentially says, "You don't know the way, but I do. Follow Me."

We too walk roads we have never walked before. New seasons, new challenges, paths with no map. And to every one of us God says the same thing: keep your eyes on My presence, and I will lead you through. We do not need to know the whole way. We only need to follow the One who does.

Yet notice the second instruction: "keep a distance... do not go near it." God's presence led them, but it was also holy. There was a healthy reverence, a recognition that the God who guides is also the God who is utterly holy. Familiarity was never to slide into carelessness.

We come to God through Christ with wonderful nearness and confidence (Heb 4:16), yet never with flippancy. He is our loving Father and our holy God at once. We follow Him closely in love, and we bow before Him in awe.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What unfamiliar road are you walking that requires you to follow God closely?
2. Do you hold together both nearness to God and reverence for His holiness?
3. How does it comfort you that God knows the way even when you don't?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I have never walked this way before, but You have. Help me follow Your presence closely, with love and holy reverence together. Amen.
